title: I Took the Community-Unicycle Checkout to the Coach Who Skipped the Pedal Log

parts.text: I stepped into gym floor at 5:06 p.m. and coach Nils was already using my numbered unicycle. The board said: FORTY MINUTES. PEDALS STAY IN THE LOG. I was twenty-three, circus intern, holding a clipboard that listed our drill. Nils shrugged. "Coaches keep the wheel." I photographed the board, the booking, and his feet on my pedals. Then I asked for the pedal log. At 5:14 the circus desk pinged why Nils's feet sat on our pedals. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The circus desk can see Nils on the gym floor during our drill.

social.video_title: He skipped the pedal log on my numbered unicycle — Part 1/2
social.description: Community unicycle, a coach on my pedals, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the feet. Would you have asked for the pedal log?

parts.text: Nils called it idling until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the pedal still. The unicycle went back to my numbered hook. Nils ran a slot of their own and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COACHES DO NOT KEEP THE WHEEL. I keep our drill on a labeled card. Nils brown-bags his idling. The gym finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches do not keep the wheel — Part 2/2
social.description: Pedal log, numbered unicycle, and a second line on the board. Was idling ever our drill?
